---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Inventory Margin Compression
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(invt, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Above-industry gross-profit firms that accumulate inventory while gross margins contract earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates whether the strong inventory-divergence evidence reflects margin deterioration rather than merely weak growth in gross-profit dollars. Simultaneous inventory commitment and margin compression indicate that profitable firms may be building stock despite deteriorating unit economics, a mismatch not captured by unconditional inventory growth.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Maintenance-Balanced Cash Generator
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ppent))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent cash generators whose capital expenditures remain close to depreciation earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Capex near depreciation represents maintenance discipline: the firm is neither aggressively expanding nor allowing its productive base to decay. This nonmonotonic investment channel repairs the assumption that ever-lower investment is always desirable and may avoid the asset-stripping firms that weakened the portfolio evidence for the earlier renewal signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Capacity Utilization Slippage
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(capx, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(sale, ppent), 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistently profitable firms that increase capital expenditures while sales generated per unit of PPE decline earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Continued investment is particularly suspect when existing productive capacity is becoming less effective at generating sales. Requiring both higher capex and declining capacity utilization distinguishes an emerging capital overhang from the unconditional capital-investment anomaly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Short-Funded Capacity Expansion
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ppegt, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitable firms that expand gross productive capacity while increasing short-term debt earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Investors may reward the combination of profitability and capacity growth without fully pricing the refinancing risk created when expansion coincides with short-maturity borrowing. The conjunction requires a real increase in gross capacity and a simultaneous increase in current debt, rather than reducing to either investment growth or net issuance alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Peak-Profit Capex Lag
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, at), 5)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Historically profitable firms whose capex is near its own historical high after profitability has fallen below its historical peak earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Investment plans often lag operating conditions, creating overcommitment when spending remains elevated after peak profitability has passed. Firm-specific historical position and peak distance test this delayed adjustment mechanism more directly than contemporaneous capex growth or a short profitability trend.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Aging Asset Harvest Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ppent)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(ppegt, ppent), 3), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-profitable firms that spend below depreciation while their productive asset base becomes progressively older earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Low investment can represent unsustainable harvesting rather than discipline when gross PPE rises relative to net PPE, indicating an aging asset base. This interaction directly tests whether apparent cash-cow profitability is temporarily inflated by deferred replacement, helping diagnose why a simple profitability-plus-low-investment conjunction failed to produce positive portfolio alpha.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Inventory Margin Compression---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a near-clone of the archived "Profitable Inventory Divergence" (identical conditioning gate, identical inventory-growth leg, only the second leg swapped from gross-profit-change-to-assets to gross-margin change), i.e., precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and both legs also lean on the already-published inventory-growth and margin-deterioration anomalies.

---CRITIQUE Maintenance-Balanced Cash Generator---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The absolute-deviation-from-maintenance-capex leg is a genuinely non-monotonic reformulation of the investment channel (not just "less capex is better"), it is internally consistent with the positive expected sign, and it plausibly diagnoses the asset-stripping contamination that flipped the earlier Renewal Surplus portfolio evidence — though the ABS(capx−dp)/ppent term will be very noisy for asset-light firms even after winsorization.

---CRITIQUE Capacity Utilization Slippage---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The two legs are mechanically entangled — rising capex directly inflates the ppent denominator of sale/ppent, so "declining sales per unit of PPE" is partly implied by the first leg, meaning the conjunction risks collapsing into a double-counted investment-growth (asset-growth anomaly) signal rather than the claimed independent utilization channel.

---CRITIQUE Short-Funded Capacity Expansion---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent and economically coherent, and debt-maturity funding is a substantively different channel from the archived equity-funded version, but it reuses that signal's exact template and both legs are close cousins of the well-documented asset-growth and net-debt-issuance anomalies, so incremental novelty is modest.

---CRITIQUE Peak-Profit Capex Lag---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Expression matches the hypothesis and sign (high MIN = capex near own 5-year high while profitability sits well below its own peak), and using firm-specific historical position/peak distance rather than short-window ACCEL/TREND is a real measurement change from the archived Post-Peak Capex Commitment, not a relabeling.

---CRITIQUE Aging Asset Harvest Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The aging proxy is largely an accounting consequence of the first leg — sustained capex below depreciation mechanically raises accumulated depreciation and hence ppegt/ppent — so the "conjunction" is substantially redundant and may simply re-sort the same underinvestment variable that already failed to deliver alpha, even though the diagnostic motivation is sensible.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Short-Debt Interest Squeeze
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(xint, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistently profitable firms that increase short-term borrowing while interest expense rises earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The signal captures realized refinancing pressure rather than substituting another operating-investment variable into the inventory-divergence template. Requiring both current-debt growth and a contemporaneous increase in interest cost distinguishes costly financing deterioration from debt issuance alone and retains broad balance-sheet coverage.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Lagged Capex Demand Failure
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(DELTA(capx, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(sale, 1), LAG(at, 1))), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistently profitable firms whose prior increase in capital spending is followed by weak sales realization earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Lagging the capex commitment and measuring demand with sales change scaled by assets removes the mechanical denominator link between current capex and sales per PPE. The interaction identifies expansion programs that fail to generate subsequent demand even though profitability from the established business remains strong.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Undermaintenance Profit Erosion
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_ADJ(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), 0), MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(capx, dp), ppent)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-profitable firms that invest below depreciation while operating profitability trends downward earn lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: A high signal now requires an independently observed deterioration in operating profitability rather than an aging measure mechanically produced by low capex. This distinguishes sustainable investment restraint from asset harvesting that is already impairing the underlying earnings engine, directly addressing the portfolio failure of unconditional low-investment cash-cow signals.
